text:
Montreal arrives at Winnipeg's door with its best two centers' worth of problems and a good recent stretch. The Canadiens are 3-1-1 in their last five after a 4-1 win in Chicago on Friday, and they're doing it without Nick Suzuki and Ivan Demidov. Oliver Kapanen has stepped in beside Juraj Slafkovský and Cole Caufield, and Jake Evans is up to 17:12 a night. The Jets are winless in four (0-2-2) after a 3-2 overtime loss in Dallas, and without Josh Morrissey, Neal Pionk is playing 25:50 a night. Our numbers say the slump is real: Winnipeg has had 45% of the expected goals, a measure of chance quality, over that stretch.

Montreal has controlled more of the play at five on five (54% of expected goals to Winnipeg's 46%), and we make it a close game, 3.14 expected goals to 3.01 for the Jets. Winnipeg's power play (0.56 expected goals a game) tops Montreal's (0.47), and Montreal has taken 5.5 penalties a game, which keeps feeding it. In net, projected starters Jacob Fowler (+3.2 goals saved above expected, meaning saves beyond what the shots deserved) and Stuart Skinner (+5.1) are both off to good starts. Skinner was +5.96 last season over 50 games, Fowler +5.98 over 17.

Kyle Connor is our top scoring pick at 45%, and Caufield leads Montreal at 39%. Slafkovský, the first overall pick in 2022, is at 61% for a point. Our under-the-radar pick is Winnipeg's Cole Perfetti, 55% for a point against a season pace of 46%, because his line creates chances (3.97 expected goals per 60 with him on the ice). He's a player to watch, not a lock.
